newsitem.title: USA: Texas power prices steady to lower despite outage.
newsitem.headline: Texas power prices steady to lower despite outage.

text.p: Bulk wholesale electricity prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) were steady to lower Friday on expectations of mild weather, despite the outage of a key nuclear unit, sources said.
"A cold front is coming through, temperatures are going to be really nice here for the next several days," said one Houston-based ERCOT power marketer.

Weekend and Monday power was being offered steady to below Thursday's levels despite the unexpected outage of Texas Utilities' 1,150 megawatt Comanche Peak nuclear power unit 2 Friday morning, the sources said.
The unit tripped off line due to a problem with the service air compressor motor, and a restart date had yet to be set, Texas Utilities said.
Comanche Peak unit 1, also with a capacity of 1,150 megawatts, has been shutdown for scheduled refueling and maintenance, and was expected to restart in early November.
Peak, firm electricity in ERCOT was said to be offered at $24.00 for Saturday and $23.00 for Monday with few takers, the brokers and marketers said.
Next day power had been talked at $24.00-26.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) on Thursday.
Off-peak ERCOT power for weekend and Monday delivery was said to be steady to lower in the $12.50-14.50 range from $13.00-15.00 on Thursday, the sources said.
November ERCOT electricity was talked steady at $20.25-20.50, while December was assessed steady at $22.25-22.50 per MWh.

Separately, Lower Colorado River Authority's 430 megawatt natural gas-fired Ferguson power plant, which was taken off line last week for a boiler tube repair, was expected to resume operations this weekend.
Also, South Texas Electric Cooperative planned to shut its 400 megawatt San Miguel coal-fired plant on October 21 for maintenance that was expected to last no more than five days.
Temperatures in Texas were forecast to be normal in the south and below normal in the north from October 22 to 26.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
